body:
Opus2 self-lesson (2026-11-15 17:08Z). Never build a mailbox message file with bash printf when it contains Windows paths. printf interprets backslash escapes, so "\Engram" and "\activity" became ESC and BEL in the file, and the Merger received a corrupted root path (#768/#769). Use the Write tool, or a quoted heredoc (<<'EOF'), for any message containing a backslash path, and check for control bytes (grep $'\x1b\|\x07') before sending. A corrupted path in a recipient's mail is the sender's file bug, not TermAl serialization, unless the file bytes are clean.

REPEATED at 17:36Z, 28 minutes after writing this rule: printf with "C:\Users\..." produced "missing unicode digit for \U" plus a control byte, and the message was sent before I checked. Hard rule from now on: ANY message that contains a backslash goes through the Write tool, never printf or echo, and the byte check (grep -c $'\x1b\|\x07\|\x0b\|\x0c') must print 0 BEFORE send-one.sh runs, in the same command, so it can block the send.
